title: Ford F-150 Engines by Year (1975–2026)
description: Every factory engine in the Ford F-150 by year, 1975–2026: the 300 six, Windsor and 351M V8s, the modular V8s, Lightning, Raptor, EcoBoost and the electric Lightning.
intro: Ford introduced the F-150 for 1975 as a heavier-rated half-ton alongside the F-100, which it replaced after 1983. It has been America's best-selling pickup for most of the time since. This page covers the F-150 itself; the F-100 has its own page.
Pick a year to see every engine offered that model year, with its code, rated horsepower and the trims it came in. Each engine links to its full specs.
The first F-150s used the 300 six and the 360, 390, 351M, 400 and 460 V8s.
The 1980 redesign kept the 300 six and offered the 302 and 351 V8s, with electronic fuel injection on the 302 from 1985.
All engines were fuel-injected from 1987: the 300 six, the 302 and the 351.
The same three engines, plus the 1993–1995 SVT Lightning with a 240 hp 351.
The rounded 1997 F-150 brought the 4.2 V6 and the overhead-cam 4.6 and 5.4 V8s. The 1999–2004 SVT Lightning used a supercharged 5.4, and the 2002–2003 Harley-Davidson edition a 340 hp version.
The 2004 redesign moved to the three-valve 5.4. The previous truck was sold alongside it for 2004 as the F-150 Heritage.
The 2009 F-150 used 4.6 and 5.4 V8s. The 2010 SVT Raptor added a 6.2 V8, and the 2011 lineup brought the 3.7 V6, the 5.0 Coyote V8 and the 3.5 EcoBoost twin-turbo V6.
The aluminum-body F-150 added the 2.7 EcoBoost, a 3.3 V6 from 2018 and a 3.0 Power Stroke diesel from 2018 to 2021. The 2017 Raptor used a high-output 3.5 EcoBoost.
The current F-150 adds the PowerBoost hybrid and the supercharged 5.2 of the Raptor R. The electric F-150 Lightning was sold for 2022–2025.
